question: Should this known-regressing contingency rollback remain as an open draft, or should it be closed and recreated only when a post-deploy incident supplies evidence that the current-main fix must be reverted?
rationale: The branch intentionally reintroduces a production publication failure, so preserving it as an incident-only artifact versus closing it is an operational ownership decision rather than a code-correctness choice.

options.title: Close until an incident requires it
options.body: Close the draft now and recreate a narrow rollback from the recorded fix commit only if a new incident establishes that reverting current-main behavior is necessary.

options.title: Retain as an incident-only draft
options.body: Keep it draft-only with an explicit incident owner and require fresh evidence, rollback scope, and recovery steps before any merge approval.

recommendation.title: Close until an incident requires it
recommendation.body: Close the draft now and recreate a narrow rollback from the recorded fix commit only if a new incident establishes that reverting current-main behavior is necessary.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current-main repair and this exact rollback proposal, so they have the clearest documented context for the affected publication topology.
